area.title: Templates
area.scope: Notification templates: the manage templates list, creating a template (type, name, answers in template mode, review, save, untitled, discard), viewing a saved template, changing a section, editing, using a template to start a notification, and deleting a template. No real service has templates today. The high-risk plants frontend has no templates today; its ledger's parked reuse-previous-consignment ruling (d-038) is here.

sources.role: the answers to the two notification view header questions the 25 November re-distil raised from ruling:sam-2026-11-19 point 2. It settles c-438: once the amend confirmation page exists, 'Amend this notification' on the header is a link to that page rather than a posting button, because the first click then changes nothing, a POST that only renders a page is the wrong verb and leaves a re-POST on the back button without JavaScript, and Delete already opens its confirmation page by href in the same header; Copy as new keeps its own form because it still changes something, Delete stays a link, and no action shares another's form, in live animals, germinal products and plants alike. Point 2 of the 19 November ruling is unweakened, its subject being that no action shares another action's form, which a link does not do. It settles c-447 the other way from the default: the plants header gains a Copy as new action so both journeys offer the same three actions. That is wiring rather than a feature build, because every layer beneath it is already on main - the plants backend serves POST /{referenceNumber}/copy with a NotificationCopyMapper, the plants frontend's real and stub persistence both implement copy, and its engine holds copyJourney - and only the header's copyAction and route are missing. The plants backend therefore needs nothing and trade-imports-plants-backend does not join this programme's repos; inc-123 takes plantsfrontend alongside backend, frontend and tests, and inc-124's stale-copy return takes plants too. Plants' copy carries plants' own answers, so the carried-over-trade against cleared-shipment split is read against plants' own fields rather than copied field for field.

sources.role: the decision that pagination is kept everywhere and that its earlier removal was an error: every address book list and every address picker pages, and no requirement says a list of an organisation's addresses is served or shown unpaginated. It drops req-611's 'unpaginated' clause and supersedes ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6 on that point alone, because that point's reasoning rested on the address book's list endpoint taking no role and so having to be read whole and paged for display, which is no longer true of the service: RequestedListFilters takes roles and searchRoles, AddressController lists one page at a time with page and pageSize, and ListPaging sets 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, exactly the bounds ruling:paul-2026-11-05 point 8 names. The role filter runs in the service before the page is cut, so paging the API cannot make it wrong, and Paul's point 8 stands in full. The rest of ruling:ian-2026-11-23 stands: the pickers page at eight, the one-page clause of inc-087's criteria 7, 8 and 9 stays dropped with req-594 and req-595, and the 'Selected address' restatement comes back with the paging. EUDPA-827 is the fix and has landed on the animals frontend's main. It settles conflict c-292 by keeping the plants contact picker's pagination and inset, and the contact picker pages at eight rather than five, confirmed by Ian the same day, so every picker in both journeys pages at the figure the INS address book list already uses and ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 1 set for the other pickers.

sources.role: the decision on transporter management, outranking ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm on that point and lifting claim c-285: the address book manages transporters as per-organisation records, and adding one mid journey uses the address book hand-off already built for addresses (inc-077, inc-078, inc-080). A transporter is its own record in its own transporters collection inside the address book service, not the Address model; it has no roles and stores a private-or-commercial type instead; a commercial transporter country is forced to XI (Northern Ireland) with no reference-data lookup, while a private transporter keeps its choice of export country. Approved transporters are parked.

claims.statement: This ruling settles whether the service manages transporters at all and, if so, whether the address book or something else does - the question ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm point 5 (claim c-285) left blocked pending requirements.
claims.quote: On transporter management, which Sam's ruling of 9 October (afternoon) left blocked pending requirements — whether the service manages transporters at all and, if so, whether the address book or something else does (`ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm` point 5, claim c-285):
claims.note: answers the block ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm point 5 left, recorded there as claim c-285

claims.statement: The address book manages transporters, which are saved per organisation just like other addresses.
claims.quote: My decision is that the address book will manage the transporters, just like other addresses which are saved per organisation.

claims.statement: Adding a transporter uses the same pattern of moving to the address book mid journey that adding other addresses uses.
claims.quote: It will use the same pattern with moving to the address book mid journey, like other addresses when adding transporters - it's essentially the same pattern.

claims.statement: The earlier block rested on the concept of 'approved transporters': a list that may be managed in MDM for all organisations and added to each organisation's own transporter options.
claims.quote: I think that previous ruling was based on the concept of 'approved transporters' which may be a list managed in MDM for all organisations that will be added to the organisations individual transporter options.

claims.statement: Approved transporters are not to be worried about for now.

sources.role: the decision on what the address book stores for an address's type and uses (EUDPA-711): "use" is renamed "role" everywhere, in the record, the API, the code, the copy keys, the tests and the spec, and an address holds the roles it can play on a notification, being place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer, place of destination and branch address. The address book stores roles only and requires at least one; it does not store an address type and ignores one a client sends, the address type being the INS front door's grouping of roles worked out from them. The grouping of roles into sending, receiving and branch is the address book's internal rule rather than part of its API, and it refuses roles from more than one group, and a consignee, importer or place of destination outside the United Kingdom. The list takes role, repeatable and any-of, and searchRole, in place of addressType, use and searchUse. A role a new notification type needs is added in code, each role in exactly one group. Addresses saved before the change are not migrated: after release the addresses collection is dropped in dev and test with CDP tooling and the address book restarted, and locally the stack is restarted. The address book's list and every address picker keep pagination even though the Design Release 2.1 prototype has none, the list API paging with page and pageSize of 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, because organisations in test environments hold thousands of addresses; no requirement to list an organisation's addresses unpaginated is built, which ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6 later reads the other way for req-611 and so outranks on that point alone.

sources.role: the owner's decisions: outranks every other source. Search boxes use the real frontend's accessible component with MDM's entries. JavaScript behaviour follows the toolbox rule with graceful degradation; JavaScript-only prototype behaviour, pop-ups included, waits on design in its own theme. Commodity catalogue and search wait on MDM; transporter management waits on requirements; the INS dashboard's summary information waits on its requirements. The overview, review, declaration and confirmation are set-owned, and shared parts change add-only. Where plants has the same page or behaviour, the same increment changes it. Each notification list is reframed in its own frontend. The report groups work as ready or blocked. Claims marked as the orchestrator's apply Sam's principles and are not his rulings; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates covers templates and the dashboard narrowing.

claims.statement: Sam rules that, as a pre-step for these increments, three questions are answered: is it possible with off-the-shelf GDS; if not, with other complementary off-the-shelf components; if not, why is the atypical thing strongly required. claims.statement: Increments are grouped into themes, and the themes are drawn from the evidence.
claims.quote: Themes: group the increments into themes based on the evidence.

claims.statement: Each theme's boundary is set by the code it touches.
claims.quote: Draw the boundaries by the code each one touches
claims.note: New.

claims.quote: so themes can be built in parallel on separate machines without conflicting PRs.

claims.statement: The ruling's DR1 paragraph has an elision marked [...]: what the omitted words said about the DR1 parity backlog is not recorded.
The ruling does not say what makes a difference 'truly exceptional', so when a question for people is warranted is left open.

The ruling limits DR1 use to clashes between 'the real frontend' and the prototype; it does not say which frontend that is, or whether DR1 judgements apply to differences in the INS frontend, the backends or other repos.
The ruling does not say which override wins when a DR1 judgement and a real constraint the prototype cannot express point different ways on the same difference.
The ruling does not say what a real service does where a real constraint overrides the prototype: whether it keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as the constraint allows.
The ruling does not say whether a feature or behaviour a real service has that Design Release 2.1 does not show at all counts as a difference to remove, or is left alone.
The ruling does not say what to do where the code two themes need to touch overlaps, so no boundary keeps their pull requests from conflicting.

await answerOrigin(page, { search: 'Irel', country: 'Republic of Ireland' })
      await answerCommodity(page, SPECIES.cattle)
claims.note: Inferred: no other section is answered before the review form's submit saves the template.

claims.statement: Submitting the template review form saves the template and returns to /templates.
claims.quote:
await page.locator('main form[action$="/review-notification"] button[type="submit"]').first().click()
      await expect(page).toHaveURL(urlFor('/templates'))
claims.note: The submit button's text on the template review page is not asserted.

claims.statement: After a new template is saved, the manage templates page shows a notification banner '<template name> saved to templates', such as 'Weekly Irish cattle saved to templates'.
claims.quote: await expect(page.locator('.govuk-notification-banner')).toContainText('Weekly Irish cattle saved to templates')

claims.statement: A saved new template joins the list: the count rises to 'Show 1-16 of 16 results'.
claims.quote: await expect(page.locator('main')).toContainText('Show 1-16 of 16 results')

claims.statement: Opening /templates/create?new=1 directly starts a new template at the notification type question.
claims.quote:
await page.goto(url('/templates/create?new=1'))
    await page.locator('input[name="notificationType"][value="live-animals"]').check()
claims.note: Inferred: the test checks a notificationType radio right after going to the URL, so it lands on the type page as p8-052 shows.

claims.statement: The template name is optional: pressing 'Save and continue' with no name moves on to /origin-of-the-import with no error.
claims.ref: e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:174-179 (create a new template › a template with no name is saved as "Untitled template")
claims.quote:
await saveAndContinue(page)
    await submitForm(page, 'Save and continue')
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(urlFor('/origin-of-the-import'))

claims.statement: Opening /templates/save during a template journey saves the template and returns to /templates.
claims.quote:
await page.goto(url('/templates/save'))
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(urlFor('/templates'))
claims.note: No page link to /templates/save is asserted; the review form submit (p8-067) may post there.

claims.statement: A template saved with no name is called 'Untitled template', and the banner reads 'Untitled template saved to templates'.
claims.quote: await expect(page.locator('.govuk-notification-banner')).toContainText('Untitled template saved to templates')

claims.statement: No validation error is proven for the template name page: no test asserts a rule such as a maximum length or a duplicate name.
claims.note: Looked at every test that fills or skips the name field; none uses expectErrorSummary or expectInlineError.

claims.statement: During a template journey, /templates/discard shows a discard confirmation headed 'Delete this template?'.
claims.ref: e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:185-193 (create a new template › discard a template being created)
claims.quote:
await page.goto(url('/templates/discard'))
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(urlFor('/templates/discard'))
    await expectHeading(page, 'Delete this template?')
claims.note: No page link to /templates/discard is asserted; how a user reaches it is not shown.

claims.statement: The discard confirmation shows the name of the template being created, such as 'Name Throwaway'.
claims.quote: await expect(page.locator('main')).toContainText(/Name\s+Throwaway/)

claims.statement: The discard confirmation's back link goes to /review-notification.
claims.quote: await expectBackLink(page, url('/review-notification'))

claims.statement: Pressing 'Yes, delete' on the discard confirmation discards the template being created and returns to /templates.
claims.quote:
await submitForm(page, 'Yes, delete')
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(urlFor('/templates'))

claims.statement: After a template being created is discarded, the manage templates page shows a banner '<template name> has been deleted', such as 'Throwaway has been deleted'.
claims.quote: await expect(page.locator('.govuk-notification-banner')).toContainText('Throwaway has been deleted')

claims.statement: Opening /templates/discard outside a template journey redirects to the manage templates page at /templates.
claims.ref: e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:202-205 (create a new template › the discard page outside a template journey returns to manage templates)
claims.quote:
await page.goto(url('/templates/discard'))
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(urlFor('/templates'))

claims.statement: Only a live animals template is proven: every template test chooses the live-animals notification type, and no other type's template is exercised.
claims.note: Whether templates for germinal products or other types behave the same is not shown.

claims.statement: Only the first section's Change link (origin) is exercised; the template review mode of other sections' pages, and where their Save and return leads, is unproven.
A template's task list shows the word 'Template' followed by the template's name, such as 'Template Arena Aintree'.
claims.ref: e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:92 (a saved template › edit: opens the template on its own task list)
claims.quote: await expect(main).toContainText(/Template\s+Arena Aintree/)
claims.note: Replaces p8-036 without its unasserted 'in place of a status and reference'. The same pattern holds for a new template ('Template Weekly Irish cattle', line 149).
